title: Windows and Doors Rebates in Mississauga 2026: Home Renovation Savings
desc: Mississauga window and door rebates for 2026: $100 per rough opening, who qualifies among 244,575 households and how to plan a bundle.
h1: Windows and Doors Rebates in Mississauga
lead: Mississauga has 244,575 households, and 70% own. Windows are the smallest rebate in the assessment stream, so this page is about when they are worth including.
cards_heading: What the Home Renovation Savings program pays for windows and doors in Mississauga
cards_intro: We re-read the program's page and its eligibility requirements on October 3, 2026. Windows and doors are paid only inside the assessment stream, so every amount here comes with an assessment and at least two upgrades.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: One payment per opening in an outside wall, not per unit. A bay window with three panes in one opening earns $100.

cards.title: Smallest qualifying job
cards.note: Three window openings, or one door, sliding door or skylight opening, count as one qualified measure. Two windows alone earn nothing.

cards.title: Home energy assessment
cards.note: Covers the cost of the first and the follow-up assessment once the program is completed.

cards.title: Three or more upgrades
cards.note: Windows count as one upgrade. Insulation, air sealing and a heat pump water heater are the others in this stream.

cards.title: Program cap
cards.note: $10,000 for homes heated by electricity, oil, propane or wood, and $5,000 for homes heated by Enbridge gas.

after_cards: The program is run by Enbridge Gas and Save on Energy. Post-audits must be scheduled by November 30, 2026 and completed by December 31, 2026, or within 180 days of your first assessment, whichever comes first.
sections: In the 2021 Census 70% of Mississauga households own, but only 37% live in a single detached house, and 27% live in apartments of five or more storeys. 62% live in a house type the program covers. The eligible pool is smaller than the owner figure suggests, because owning a condo does not make a household eligible: condos and apartments are not covered.
Mid-century homes and the window question

38% of Mississauga households live in homes built before 1981, and 30,140 are owner-occupied detached houses. Major repairs were reported by 4.8%. For those houses, the rebate for windows is a small part of the total bill, so use it as the third upgrade to unlock the $500 bonus rather than as the reason to replace.

The rebate pays by rough opening. A wall with a large fixed window and two side vents in one frame is one opening. A door with sidelights in one frame is also one opening. Ask for the number in writing, and ask whether any units share a frame. A sliding door counts as a door-type opening and qualifies alone.

Skylights and sliding doors are treated as openings too. One sliding door is enough to count as a qualifying measure by itself, and so is one skylight. That makes a patio door the cheapest way to clear the minimum in many Mississauga houses, although the rebate is the same $100 as for a window, and the audit still has to happen first.

The program requires you to own the home. Where an owner has tenants in part of the house, the owner must apply. In a Mississauga house with a rented basement, that means the owner books the audits and signs the participant agreement, and the audit must cover the whole home with a central heating system.
claim_steps: Confirm you own the home, it has been occupied for six months and it is one of the eligible house types.
Book the first home energy assessment with a registered energy advisor before any work starts.
Choose at least one more upgrade to pair with the windows, and get quotes that count rough openings the way the program does.
Ask the energy advisor to confirm the opening count on the custom report.
Have a professional install complete windows or doors with frames, keep the ENERGY STAR labels on until the follow-up assessment, and book it.
